result.title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
result.summary: Language-model reasoning alternates between sustained activities and local operations. We study how this temporal structure predicts continuation and the computation needed to analyze it. T/E/S combines text, local events, and spans of activity. Across reasoning and information-seeking tasks, events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in 70 of 76 evaluation groups for a Transformer and 74 of 76 for Qwen with LoRA. Span duration and preceding events are associated with transitions, and retaining event history across span boundaries improves prediction. We formulate budget-allocation counting and action-conditional continuation queries, prove counting hardness under explicit encodings, and derive conditions for affordable decision certification. In finite-process experiments, bounds that cancel shared continuation mass recover the same optimal actions as full dynamic programming while reducing mean inference CPU time by 77.7%. On 71 held-out HotpotQA and MuSiQue questions, a compact structural observer improves prediction of whether a fixed inference procedure finishes within a CPU allowance: Brier loss falls from 0.0836 to 0.0756. An annotation audit identifies substantial errors in that observer, separating this computational result from semantic validation of its features.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 T/E/S 结构表示，用文本、局部事件与活动跨度刻画 LLM 推理的时间结构，在推理与信息检索任务上预测后续结果；并形式化预算分配计数与动作条件延续查询，用可消去共享延续质量的界剪枝动态规划，在 HotpotQA/MuSiQue 上预测固定推理流程能否在 CPU 预算内完成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其事件—跨度状态表示与「还要多少计算、是否继续」的预算分配和停止判定，可能为 LVR 的 THINK/STOP 收益成本预测提供方法线索；但工作为纯文本且作者自述观察器标注错误较多，特征语义可供核查。
